segments.script: First, meaning. I read “He had spoken the very truth, and transformed it into the veriest falsehood” slowly and put it in my own words: Dimmesdale tells his congregation that he is a vile sinner, but they take his words as proof of his holy humility. Next, craft. I notice the paradox "spoken the very truth, and transformed it into the veriest falsehood," which sets truth and lie side by side. The strongest word is “falsehood”: it shows how a true statement, made vaguely, becomes a lie. Then, effect. Why does Dimmesdale's public confession make his guilt worse?
